2_Introduction: The PSCs achieved a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.8426%, with VOC of 1.1082 V, FF of 74.2331%, and JSC of 25.335 mA/cm². For the inorganic perovskite layers, 1.6 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.05FA0.9PbI3.0 inorganic perovskite precursor solution was prepared in DMF/DMSO solvent. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s, respectively. During the second step, antisolvent CB (150 µL) was dropped at the middle of the spinning substrate 10 s prior to the end of the spinning. Then the film was annealed at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₅FA₀.₉PbI₃.₀ inorganic perovskite layer—governed by the delicate interplay among A-site cation mixing (where FA⁺ provides structural stability and optimal Goldschmidt tolerance factor ~0.98, Cs⁺ suppresses δ-phase formation and thermal-induced halide segregation, and trace MA⁺ kinetically enhances nucleation without compromising phase purity), PbI₂-rich stoichiometry, and solvent engineering—proceeds through a tightly controlled intermediate phase evolution: the DMF/DMSO cosolvent system stabilizes soluble [PbI₆]⁴⁻ octahedral complexes, while the precisely timed antisolvent quenching at 10 s before spin cessation induces instantaneous supersaturation, triggering homogeneous nucleation across the substrate and suppressing uncontrolled Ostwald ripening; this, combined with the moderate 110 °C/15 min thermal annealing, enables full ligand expulsion and grain coalescence without excessive volatilization of FA⁺ or iodide loss, yielding large, oriented grains with low intragrain strain—as corroborated by the absence of residual PbI₂ peaks at ~12.6° and narrow XRD FWHM of the (110) reflection—thereby minimizing trap-assisted recombination at grain boundaries and within the bulk. Although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance arises from the synergistic A-site alloying: Cs⁺ rigidifies the lattice and reduces halide vacancy formation energy, MA⁺ transiently lowers the activation barrier for crystallographic reorientation during annealing, and FA⁺ dominates the final lattice framework to maintain high dielectric screening and suppress ion migration, collectively enhancing carrier lifetime and reducing non-radiative voltage losses. Critically, the high PCE is underpinned by morphological and structural evidence: uniform film coverage and high optical contrast in grayscale intensity maps confirm continuous, pinhole-free morphology essential for lateral charge extraction, while the absence of localized PL quenching spots and elevated average PL intensity—indicative of suppressed non-radiative decay pathways—directly reflect the low density of deep-level traps at surfaces and grain boundaries, consistent with the XRD-confirmed phase-pure α-perovskite structure and minimal lattice strain. These interlinked crystallization control, intrinsic compositional passivation, and structural homogeneity culminate in VOC of 1.1082 V, JSC of 25.335 mA/cm², FF of 74.2331%, and PCE of 20.8426%.
